title: Quadratic generation of matroid toric ideals: the weak White conjecture
statement: For every finite matroid M of positive rank on [n], with set of bases B(M), let phi: Q[y_B : B in B(M)] -> Q[x_1,...,x_n] send y_B to the product of x_i for i in B. Is ker(phi) generated by homogeneous quadratic binomials? All quadratic binomials preserving element multiplicities are allowed; the claim does not require symmetric-exchange generators or a quadratic Gröbner basis.
source_locator: SRC-MATH-104, Conjecture 1.1(3) and its toric-ideal interpretation; SRC-MATH-105, Conjecture 1.1.
status_basis: The June 2026 source explicitly states quadratic generation as a conjecture. The July 2026 source separates it from the symmetric-exchange version it disproves and reports no counterexample to this weak version. A targeted update search found no later resolution, which is not proof of global open status.

relations.explanation: The Fano audit concerns a stronger Gröbner-basis property. Its failure does not imply failure of arbitrary quadratic generation.

plain_summary: Ask whether every algebraic relation among matroid bases can be built from relations involving just two bases at a time. Recent counterexamples to stronger statements make the exact choice of permitted moves essential.
assumptions: M is a finite matroid of positive rank on the labeled ground set [n]; loops and parallel elements are allowed.
There is one indeterminate y_B for each distinct basis; the coefficient field in this card is Q.
A permitted quadratic replaces two bases A,B by two bases C,D whenever their element-count vectors agree, with repetitions allowed.
The question is generation as an ideal; it imposes no term order and no requirement that each move be a single symmetric exchange.
scope: The weak quadratic-generation version for arbitrary finite matroids. It is not bounded by rank or ground-set size and is not classified as a cheap exhaustive-search task.
target: A proof for all finite matroids under this formulation, a fully verified counterexample, or a clearly delimited intermediate result whose novelty is separately checked.
success_criteria: For a positive resolution, prove ideal generation for every finite matroid, not merely for examined instances.
For a negative resolution, specify a matroid by verifiable data and give a binomial in ker(phi) together with a certificate that it is not in the ideal generated by all allowed quadrics.
Alternatively, a finite disconnected fiber under all two-basis replacements can support a counterexample, provided the algebraic equivalence and completeness of the move graph are established.
Any partial result must name its matroid class, rank or degree restrictions and remain separate from the unrestricted status.
known_results: The inspected June 2026 paper states quadratic generation as Conjecture 1.1 and distinguishes it from the quadratic-Gröbner question.
Larson's July 2026 Conjecture 1.1 separates arbitrary quadratic moves from symmetric exchanges; Theorem 1.5 refutes the latter restriction, not the weak version targeted here.
prerequisites: Toric ideals and binomial ideal membership
Exact algebraic computation and certificate design
significance: The question links combinatorial exchange structure to the algebra of matroid base configurations. A resolution would clarify what survives after stronger exchange and Gröbner-basis claims fail.

requirements.experiment: No physical experiment; mathematical objects and exact certificates are required.
requirements.data: For computational work, explicit matroid descriptions and complete basis lists or certified independence oracles. Any external database needs a version, provenance and checks of its represented class.
requirements.compute: No general feasible resource bound is asserted. Basis sets, high-degree fibers and ideal-membership calculations can grow rapidly. Any future finite search must first declare rank, ground-set size, fiber degree, representation and stopping limits.
requirements.theoretical_assumptions: Matroid axioms over a finite ground set and the declared polynomial-ring map over Q. The field used to represent a matroid, when applicable, is distinct from the coefficient field of its toric ideal.

ai_assessment.rationale: The statement is exact and supports bounded algebraic investigations, but the unrestricted conjecture is difficult. A useful initial role is auditing variants, small certificates and candidate lemmas under expert supervision.

clarity.reason: The ring map and allowed quadratic moves remove a common ambiguity in the conjecture's name.

decomposability.reason: One can study matroid classes or fiber degrees, but success in a restricted class need not extend.

methods.reason: The sources explain several formulations and recent obstructions; their supporting literature still needs deeper review before choosing a new direction.

search_or_symbolic.reason: Finite fibers and polynomial ideals permit exact calculations once bounds and representations are fixed.

checkability.reason: An explicit finite counterexample may be checkable; arbitrary membership exclusions and universal positive arguments can be costly.

expertise.reason: The distinction among matroid exchange, ideal generation and Gröbner bases requires specialist review.

significance.reason: This is a substantive unresolved algebraic-combinatorial question according to the inspected sources.

verification_difficulty.reason: Missing quadratic moves or an incorrect algebraic equivalence can produce a false obstruction.

ai_assessment.uncertainty: The open label is source-based and dated. No AI experiment supports tractability of the unrestricted problem; source-reported computational searches do not transfer to this task or model configuration.
ai_assessment.model_scope: No named model evaluated; assumes tool-using AI with matroid theory, commutative algebra, exact computer algebra and sustained expert review.

methods: Compare equivalent fiber and ideal formulations
Exact enumeration under explicitly declared limits
Investigate selected matroid classes and structural reductions
obstacles: The same name is used for inequivalent conjectures, including variants already reported false.
Enumerating only symmetric exchanges is insufficient for this question.
Testing one degree or finitely many matroids cannot prove the universal statement.
A numerical or heuristic solver report is not a certificate of ideal nonmembership.

steps: Refresh the literature status and identify the exact weak version before starting a new attempt.
Verify the matroid axioms and the completeness of the basis representation.
Check that every quadratic preserving multiplicities is admitted in the relevant fiber graph or ideal.
Independently check the proposed algebraic proof or finite certificate and the bridge between its encoding and ker(phi).
Ask a matroid or toric-ideal specialist to assess correctness and a separate literature review to assess novelty.
validation.human_review_difficulty: High: both combinatorial and commutative-algebra expertise may be needed, especially for computational nonmembership claims.
validation.statement_alignment: The source's arbitrary two-basis replacements match the weak ideal-generation claim. Symmetric-exchange disconnection and absence of a quadratic Gröbner basis alone do not answer this card.

known_attempts: Larson reports searching for but not obtaining a counterexample to Conjecture 1.1(3). This source report is not a benchmark of the present task.
Backman and coauthors report a Fano obstruction for the stronger Gröbner-basis property.
unresolved_checks: A current specialist literature review is still needed before committing to an unrestricted attempt; no exhaustive proof of open status is possible from this check.
Original White (1980) and the cited results on special classes have not been directly inspected here.
Recent preprints and their computational artifacts need independent review before their stronger-variant results are treated as settled atlas facts.

status_search.result: The inspected June and July 2026 preprints distinguish the weak conjecture from stronger claims they discuss or refute. Targeted searches for subsequent resolution or correction found no reliable later resolution of the weak form.
status_search.limitations: A scoped web and preprint check cannot establish absence of all later work. The conservative source_reports_open status is retained; recent stronger-variant proofs were not independently reproduced.

epistemic_layers.formal_validity: Any answer must concern the exact ring map and all quadratic binomials allowed by it, with an independently checked proof or certificate.
epistemic_layers.empirical_support: No empirical claim is involved; finite computations can provide exact evidence only for their fully specified finite scope.

difficulty.basis: The unrestricted conjecture remains difficult despite compact algebraic notation; finite exploratory work requires explicit limits.

correctness.basis: No candidate answer has been submitted or independently reviewed.

novelty.basis: A future result needs a fresh comparison with the literature and an exact match to the weak conjecture.

significance.basis: A resolution would settle a central structural question about matroid toric ideals.
